blocks.content: The Constitution does not specify the number of members. The President determines the strength of the Commission.
The President determines the strength of the Commission.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Constitution does not specify the exact strength of the Union Public Service Commission.
The power to determine the number of members in the Commission rests entirely with the President.
At least half of the members must have held office for 10 or more years under the Government of India or a State Government.
Exams frequently test whether Parliament or the President determines UPSC strength — remember it is the President, as the Constitution does not specify the count.
Pay attention to member qualifications: At least HALF of the members must have a minimum of 10 years of service under the Central or State Government.

blocks.content: At least HALF of the members should have held office under the Government of India or a State Government for at least 10 years.
